title: Key Finding: Sparse Data and the Pivot to Animation
text: Identifier, and nested demographic records flattened into something analyzable. Two scripts carry the pipeline. The first flattens nested demographic structures into a single file. The second pulls six clinical categories into six: problems, encounter diagnoses, labs, social history, encounters, diagnostic reports. One piece of friction is worth naming. The repository access needed to open that pull request took a week to become usable. The invite had been sent and sat unread. Once opened, the fixes went in as a proper pull request. Retrieving the note text returned a 403 forbidden. The move that matters is not retry logic. It is reading what the server is refusing. A missing OAuth scope, system/binary.read, resolved through the developer portal. Not a defect. A permission the token never had. Then the finding that mattered more than the fix. Sparsely. That is not enough to build research on. I reported it in writing to Prof. Sridhar with a summarized spreadsheet of the sandbox API and an offer to explore further in points. Prof. Sridhar ended the Epic integration work stream citing accumulated blockers, sparse data, authorization friction, and unclear access model. Every one of them already documented from my side. The same day brought a new assignment. Manum instructional video for the physics mechanics textbook with access requested that day. Four weeks, 20 hours documented in each. 80 hours for the month. Status: in compliance. Month one, then. Two technical duties in parallel from the first week. Textbook repairs merged to the repository. A clinical data pipeline built end to end against a live API including a real authorization fix. And a data limitation found, evidenced, and escalated. Two fronts, med-heavy month one.
